text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Service latency SLO breaches detected for inference.production (p95 > 350ms) across us-west-2. Auto-page to oncall.
Maria G: seeing the page — I'm on it, grabbing traces.
SRE Jen: pinging infra, are we in the middle of any routing or cache deploys?
Jonathan: we had a small rollout 20m ago: hash-prefix tweak for KV prefixing (rollout 30%).
Eng Ravi: that was the one that changes how we build the prefix key to reduce collisions. no other infra changes.
Maria G: top symptom = big p99 spikes and a handful of streaming stalls (clients waiting for next token). p95 jumped from 120ms -> 420ms.
SRE Jen: logs show an increase in cache miss rate for prefix-store: miss_rate 0.86 -> 0.97 in the last 15m on several shards.
Maria G: confirmed. attaching quick grep: `grep "prefix_miss" /var/log/prefix/** | tail -n 50` shows repeated misses and long backend fetch times (~250ms).
Eng Ravi: hmm, the new prefix hash encodes model+prefix length differently. Might be breaking compatibility with existing prefix entries — old keys won't match.
Jonathan: rollout was supposed to be backward-compatible via dual-key lookup, but looks like that code path didn't run for older shards due to a feature flag bug.
SRE Jen: ok first quick mitigation: rollback the rollout to 0% and flip the dual-lookup flag on. @Eng Ravi can you confirm how to force the flag?
Eng Ravi: on it. command: `./deployctl set-feature prefix-dual-lookup=true --env=prod --target=us-west-2` — doing canary to avoid other surprises.
incident-bot: DEPLOY: rollback job started by Eng Ravi at 2136002502. Watch logs: https://deploys.internal/rev/8f3a
Maria G: traffic routed to older key path, but cache hit-rate hasn't recovered fully yet — some misses are TTL-expired entries from the window where new keys were written.
SRE Jen: acceptable. we'll warm the cache: starting a controlled prefetch job for top traffic routes (batch size 5000 prefixes).
Jonathan: note: some nodes still returning 404 for dual-lookup due to old runtime image. We need a coordinated restart to pick up the runtime fix. Ops can we do a rolling restart?
Eng Ravi: rolling restart set for low-traffic cooldown windows. starting node restarts in wave-1 now.
PM Ade: any customer-facing impact? which customers hit p99?
Maria G: preliminary list shows ~12 customers had tail latency >2s for <1% of requests. No error-rate increase, so correct results just slower.
PM Ade: good to know. I'll prepare a short customer note: degraded latency for a small set post-deploy; mitigation in progress.
SRE Jen: telemetry: p95 back to ~150ms after flag flip on wave-1 hosts, p99 trending down but still noisy.
incident-bot: METRIC: p95 148ms, p99 890ms (delta -60% from peak) at 2136002560.
Maria G: streaming stalls resolved for most sessions after cache warm. One remaining host showing repeated stall patterns — isolating.
Eng Ravi: found a shard with stale index files that never ingested the dual-lookup config. Re-deploying config and restarting just that shard.
SRE Jen: after restart that host's miss_rate dropped to 0.12. overall cluster hit-rate back to 0.93 (from 0.70 at peak).
Maria G: summary for postmortem: cause = feature-flag bug that prevented dual-key fallback during a prefix-hash rollout; consequence = high cache misses -> backend fetch spike -> tail latency and streaming stalls.
PM Ade: customer impact: handful of customers saw latency spikes but no failures. Support action: low-severity advisory and optional follow-up for affected accounts.
Eng Ravi: mitigations done: rollback to previous hash, forced dual-lookup enabled, rolling restarts and targeted cache warm job.
SRE Jen: next steps: postmortem, add automated integration test that verifies dual-lookup path during rollouts, and add an alert for sudden prefix miss-rate delta > 0.2.
Maria G: handing off to next oncall for follow-up at 2136002600 — please monitor p99 for 2 hours and watch the prefetch job.
Jonathan: thanks team. tagging for postmortem owners: @Eng Ravi, @SRE Jen, @Maria G.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: Oncall shift ended for Maria G at 2136002610. Handoff to SRE Jen.
SRE Jen: I'll own the monitoring window and start the post-incident notes. moving thread to #postmortems after we finalize the timeline. :white_check_mark:
